steps.text: Stir sugar, water, and cream of tartar together in a saucepan. Cook over medium-high heat until sugar is dissolved and syrup is bubbly.
Beat egg whites and vanilla in a glass, metal, or ceramic bowl until foamy. Gradually add hot syrup mixture, continuing to beat until stiff peaks form, about 7 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Fluffy White Frosting
raw_recipe.description: This fluffy, egg-white frosting is made by combining hot syrup with whipped egg whites to create a meringue-style frosting for your favorite cake.
raw_recipe.name: Fluffy White Frosting

review.reviewBody: yes!!! this is a wonderful frosting...soon to become one of my staples. When coloring, it comes out with a beautiful shine. For me, i had no cream of tartar so i used a pinch of salt in my egg whites and let it sit in them before i whipped them. The salt or cream of tartar helps to denature the egg whites so you get a better, fluffier result! PERFECT!!!

This review is for 'ALL' of the people who say that they can't get this recipe to work. I have been using a this recipe for over 40 years, and it is a beautiful frosting. It is great on all cakes, and it is soooooooo gooood!!!!!!!!! The only way to make this fail is: not cooking your sugar mixture long enough. You need to cook it until it spins a 3 to 4 inch thread, and once it starts coiling, do not stir it, and when it has cooked long enough, pour it into the stiffly beaten egg whites (while you are beating them) in a thin steady stream, and then continue to beat the frosting on high until glossy. TIP: For those who do not know about the 'spin a thread' test, just cook this for 7 minutes. That is the name of the recipe I have used forever...."Seven Minute Frosting", and it is exactly like this one.

Taking some tips gleaned from other reviews: The cook time is a lot longer. Have a glass of cold water next to you, drop the syrup in the water- if it dissolves immediately keep cooking, it is NOT ready until it forms a sugar thread as soon as it hits the water. The sugar syrup should have the thickness of corn syrup. Egg whites beat better at room temperature. I started beating my egg whites on my table top mixer w/ whisk attachment as the sugar was almost ready. As eggs start getting white and foamy, this is when you add the sugar syrup in a consistent stream. Don’t wait till you have peaks in your egg white to add the sugar syrup.

Really enjoyed this frosting. I took some frosting out at the soft peak stage of whipping and added some strawberry jam to use as as a cake filling and it came out really light and tasty. The sheen on the frosting at the hard peak stage is really pretty. It’s easy to make and not too sweet.

Light and airy, not too sweet. Just delicious. To make a chocolate version, whip the cooked syrup with the beaten egg whites according to recipe and FOLD in a 1/4 cup Hershey’s cocoa with a spatula to blend. Equally as delicious.

At last minute I decided to make icing for daughter's surprise 13 bday cupcakes, and actually started to get nervous after reading all the reviews. And I'm confident in kitchen but all this about threads and how long to boil and room temp or not...yikes. My icing came out fine...if anything maybe a little TOO stiff. 

Here's what I did: grabbed cold eggs out of frig and beat just whites with vanilla extract, as directed. Standup mixer got them to stiff peak stage in no time. I had added a little bit of almond extract, which I think tastes good but might not have been necessary. Turned off mixer and went to stove. Used smaller pot that had pour spout at lip. Medium pot seemed to big for the quantities. Got water, sugar, cream of tartar gently boiling while stirring often. Once gently boiling, set timer for 7min. Glanced at my egg whites and they had deflated and I panicked! So when about 1min left for sugar syrup, I turned mixer back on low to remix. Egg whites got to soft peak stage in that minute; left it running. Was nervous but I took small pot of hot sugar water mixture and slowly poured thin thread of hot mixture along edge of egg whites while mixer was going. Probably took 2 minutes to pour all of it in slowly. At that point reset timer for about 5-6min and let it continue mixing. Had to turn up speed as frosting thickened. Was glossy, THICK, and spread nicely. I could not just dip my cooled cupcakes into frosting, as others did. Mine too thick. A

Great recipe, my favourite.
Ran out of vanilla though, so substituted 8 tsp orange juice and 2 tsp orange rind, plus a touch of yellow food colouring. Works wonderfully on a chocolate cake, kind of like a Jaffa.

It takes a long time to get it to peak so don’t get frustrated and think it flopped it didn’t. Take your time and keep beating. You made need to use 3 egg whites instead. My first batch came out better. In a metal bowl instead of glass.

It was EASY - the cream of TarTar helps so don't miss this ingredient! I whipped the eggs to a soft peak FIRST and then added the mixture and then whipped to a firm peak - Reminds me of whipped cream frosting and actually frosted 24 cupcakes - I didn't have an icing piper, so I spooned it into a baggie and cut the corner from the bottom - Whalla!!! It was THAT easy! I added the sprinkles, and they look like I bought them from the store! LOL

Made this icing and it came out great. I was worried that by adding the food coloring would make the icing stay flat but it didn’t. I just kept mixing till it formed stiff peaks. Got compliments on the icing and this is definitely a keeper. For those who said it didn’t form stuff peaks it was probably one of two things: the syrup wasn’t hot enough (Make sure you keep mixing the simple syrup to a slow-med boil It truly needs to be hot). The other is they didn’t beat the mixture long enough. I hope this helps others in deciding to use this recipe.

Don't know what I did wrong, but it sure didn't turn out white. Used the ingredients as called for, but did not work. On second try, you have to make sure the sugar is like a thick syrup. That will do the trick. Don't just boil it and think its done, you have to really cook on med to med low for at least 10 minutes to make the sugar turn out right. Also your egg/vanilla extract mixture must be really bubbly. And you really have to add the sugar mixture really slow blending it in over a minutes time.

Once the frosting starts to boil, I let it boil for three minutes at a slow, low boil then I pour it into the egg white mixture. I also leave the lid on while it’s boiling to prevent crystallization on the side of the pan. This helps the frosting stand up better and last longer, especially in humid weather.

I tried this recipe and it is exactly what I have been searching for , I however didn’t read the instructions all the way through, I put all the ingredients in a bowl the started to mix it, then saw the bit about heating on the stove so I stop mixing and transferred to a sauce pan and heated slightly or until I saw steam rising them whisk until fluffy, thank you.
This recipe is epic. Im lactose intolerant and always cautious with the frosting i use. Not anymore now that ive found this.

I've been making this recipe for at least 50 years and my Mother made it years before that! I'm always asked for the recipe, and it's always assumed to be difficult. For me, it's more fool proof than powdered sugar frosting. I have never used vanilla, but that sounds good. For those of you having trouble: Sugar mixture (I've never used the water test)...it needs to be not only totally dissolved, but fully bubbling...be careful...so hot. You need to use a powerful mixer...pretty sure mine is on high. Add the sugar mixture...not just gradually, but VERY slowly...too fast and you'll fry the egg whites. I don't time the mixing...go by when the stiff peaks form...if your mixing on max speed after the last of sugar mixture has gone in...it won't take long. I add a little yellow food coloring for when I make banana cake, and you would swear it's banana frosting! I'm anxious to try the chocolate version several have mentioned.
Love this recipe 😋 I substituted the vanilla extract with mint extract to bake my mother's chocolate mint cupcakes, sprinkled with crushed peppermint candy cane. 🎂.
This recipe is a family favourite! I always end up with extra icing so today I turned the extra into meringue cookies. I piped them onto parchment and cooked at 300 degrees F for 20 minutes. Yum!
